what_its_for: Emgality is used to help prevent migraine headaches in adults and to treat a type of severe headache called episodic cluster headaches. It does not treat a migraine that has already started — it works in the background to reduce how often you get migraines or cluster headaches.
how_to_take: Emgality comes as a liquid in a prefilled pen or prefilled syringe that you inject under your skin (subcutaneous injection). Common injection sites are your belly (abdomen), the front of your thighs, or the back of your upper arms. Do not inject into skin that is tender, bruised, red, or hard. Rotate your injection sites each time. Before your first injection, a healthcare provider will show you how to use it properly. Always read the Instructions for Use that come with your medication.
dosing: For migraine prevention: The starting dose is 240 mg (two 120 mg injections given back-to-back one time), followed by 120 mg once every month. For episodic cluster headaches: The starting dose is 300 mg (three 100 mg injections given back-to-back) at the beginning of a cluster period, then 300 mg once every month until the cluster period ends. Your doctor will tell you exactly how many injections to give and when. Do not change your dose without talking to your doctor.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, inject it as soon as you remember. Then schedule your next dose from the date you gave that missed dose. Do not give two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are not sure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store Emgality in the refrigerator between 36°F and 46°F (2°C to 8°C). Keep it in its original carton to protect it from light. Do not freeze it — if it freezes, throw it away. If needed, you may store it at room temperature (up to 77°F / 25°C) for up to 7 days. Once it has been stored at room temperature, do not put it back in the refrigerator. Throw away any unused medication after 7 days at room temperature. Keep it out of reach of children. Do not use if the liquid looks cloudy, discolored, or contains visible particles.
what_to_avoid: There are no specific foods, drinks, or activities that you must strictly avoid while taking Emgality. However, talk to your doctor before starting any new prescription medications, over-the-counter drugs, vitamins, or herbal supplements, as interactions are possible. Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, as the effects of this medication during pregnancy are not fully known.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or get emergency help right away if you experience: signs of a serious allergic reaction such as swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat; trouble breathing or swallowing; severe rash, hives, or itching; dizziness or feeling faint. Also contact your doctor if you notice: pain, redness, swelling, or bruising at the injection site that does not go away; your headaches are not improving after several months; or you have any new or unusual symptoms. If you think you may have overdosed, call 911 or Poison Control (1-800-222-1222).
when_it_works: Emgality may start reducing the number of migraine days within the first month of treatment. However, it may take up to 3 months to see the full benefit. For cluster headaches, it may begin to help within the first week of a cluster period. Be patient and keep taking your doses as scheduled — do not stop without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: It is not known if Emgality is safe to use during pregnancy or while breastfeeding. Talk to your doctor about the risks and benefits before using this medication if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Older adults (65+): Limited information is available for this age group, but no specific dose adjustment is currently recommended. Children: Emgality is not approved for use in children or teenagers under 18 years old. Kidney or liver problems: No dose adjustment is currently recommended for mild to moderate kidney or liver issues, but always let your doctor know about any organ health concerns.
